extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies' publication/regulatory staff (liaison, certifying, authorizing officers), Office of the Federal Register staff, Government Publishing Office, and others responsible for preparing/submitting/publishing/distributing Federal Register, CFR, Government Manual, and Presidential papers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory and procedural standards governing preparation, submission, publication, citation, indexing, distribution, and subscription of the Federal Register, the Code of Federal Regulations, the United States Government Manual, and Presidential papers, and duties of agency representatives who interact with the Office of the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly list of sections affected (§ 6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A monthly list of sections of the Code of Federal Regulations affected shall be separately published on a cumulative basis during each calendar year and shall identify the sections of the Code specifically affected by documents published in the FEDERAL REGISTER during the period it covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is published separately and identifies CFR sections affected by documents published in the Federal Register for the covered period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes, digests, and guides (§ 6.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register may order the preparation and publication of indexes, digests, and similar guides, based on laws, Presidential documents, regulatory documents, and notice materials, to serve users of the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexes, digests, and guides will be published yearly or at other intervals as necessary to keep them current and useful; each is considered a special edition of the Federal Register when public need requires special printing or binding in substantial numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for the Code of Federal Regulations (§ 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall publish periodically a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER to present a compact and practical code called the 'Code of Federal Regulations' to contain each Federal regulation of general applicability and legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Committee intends every practical means be used to keep the Code current and readily usable within limitations imposed by dependability and reasonable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly development of the CFR (§ 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assure orderly development of the Code along practical lines, the Director may establish new titles and rearrange existing titles and subordinate assignments, but must consult with each agency directly affected before taking such an action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director consultation with affected agencies is required prior to reorganizing titles/assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic updating criteria for CFR (§ 8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book of the Code shall be updated at least once each calendar year; if no change has occurred, a simple notation may serve as the supplement for that year; more frequent updating may be made when content has been substantially superseded or when consistent with the Administrative Committee's intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code will be produced over a 12-month period under a staggered publication system; each updated title will reflect all amendatory documents published in the Federal Register on or before the 'As of' date (cutoff dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject index for CFR (§ 8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subject index to the entire Code shall be annually revised and separately published; agency-prepared indexes for individual books may be published with the approval of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual revision required; agency indexes allowed with Director approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary finding aids for CFR (§ 8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code shall provide finding aids including parallel tables of statutory authorities and rules, parallel tables of Presidential documents and agency rules, and a list of CFR sections affected (designed to enable users to find the precise text in effect on a given date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel tables list U.S. Code sections cited as rulemaking authority alongside parallel CFR citations; lists refer to Federal Register pages; historical 'List of CFR Sections Affected' volumes exist for past periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of publication for CFR (§ 8.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication formats authorized for the Code of Federal Regulations are: (1) Paper; (2) Microfiche; and (3) Online on GPO Access (44 U.S.C. 4101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director is authorized to regulate format according to user needs and GPO compatibility, may print in as many separately bound books as necessary, set microfiche image requirements, and oversee online organization and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cooperation in keeping CFR current (§ 8.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall cooperate in keeping publication of the Code current by complying promptly with deadlines set by the Director of the Federal Register and the Public Printer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely agency compliance with deadlines is required to maintain current publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of citation for the CFR (§ 8.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code of Federal Regulations may be cited by title and section, and the short form 'CFR' may be used (e.g., '1 CFR 10.2' refers to title 1, part 10, section 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-form citation conventions provided for clarity and uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement for The United States Government Manual (§ 9.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall separately publish annually or at times designated by the Administrative Committee a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER called 'The United States Government Manual' and may issue special supplements when such supplementation is in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication schedule set annually or as designated; supplements allowed for public interest reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the Government Manual (§ 9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual shall contain appropriate information about the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches which for major Executive agencies shall include descriptions of the agency's public purposes, programs and functions; established places and methods whereby the public may obtain information and make submittals or requests; and lists of officials heading major operating units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may also publish brief supplemental quasi-official information deemed to be of enough public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents: publication requirement (§ 10.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director publishes a special edition of the Federal Register compiling recent presidential documents, called 'The Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated as a special edition; authority and references cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and sources for Presidential documents (§ 10.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication consists of oral statements by the President or writings subscribed by the President, selected from transcripts/text issued by the White House Press Secretary and includes communications to Congress, public addresses and remarks, news conferences and interviews, public messages and letters, statements on miscellaneous subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes selections (full text or ancillary) of announcements of appointments/nominations, White House statements, Press Secretary statements, senior official statements/news conferences, and fact sheets when issued by the Press Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for the Daily Compilation (§ 10.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents is published online on the Government Printing Office access system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online publication platform specified as GPO Access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual 'Public Papers of the Presidents' publication requirement (§ 10.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall publish annually a special edition called the 'Public Papers of the Presidents of the United States'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annual compilation is based on the daily/regular compilation materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the 'Public Papers of the Presidents' (§ 10.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic text of the Public Papers consists of the documents compiled under the daily compilation subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual consolidation of the materials published regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format, indexes, and ancillaries for Public Papers (§ 10.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each publication covers one calendar year (unless procedures require otherwise), is divided into books according to material amount, and is published in binding and style the Administrative Committee considers suitable to the dignity of the Office of the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each publication is appropriately indexed and contains additional ancillary information and illustrative material respecting significant Presidential documents and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of prior years for Presidential papers (§ 10.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee may authorize publication of volumes covering specified years before 1945 after consulting with the National Historical Publications and Records Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization contingent on consultation with NHPRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriptions: production and sale (§ 11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government Printing Office produces the paper and microfiche editions described in § 2.5, and the Superintendent of Documents makes them available for sale to the public; all fees are payable in advance and they are not available for free distribution to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses payment in advance and non-free distribution policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register subscription pricing and formats (§ 11.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscription price for the paper edition of the daily Federal Register is $749/year; combined subscription pricing and microfiche pricing provided; single-copy prices based on number of pages; online edition available on GPO Access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Six-month subscriptions available at one-half annual rate; prices exclude postage; microfiche single issues may be purchased for $3 including postage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Federal Regulations subscription pricing and availability (§ 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscription price for a complete set of the CFR is $1,019/year for bound paper, or $247/year for microfiche; Government Printing Office sells individual volumes at prices determined by the Superintendent of Documents; online edition available on GPO Access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prices exclude postage; microfiche single volume price is $4 including postage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Manual availability and pricing (§ 11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the bound paper edition of the Manual are sold at a price determined by the Superintendent of Documents; the online edition is available on GPO Access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations to amendments and publication authority provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Papers sales (§ 11.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of annual clothbound volumes of the Public Papers of the Presidents are sold at a price determined by the Superintendent of Documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Price determined under general direction of the Administrative Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register Index and LSA subscription prices (§ 11.7, § 11.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual subscription price for the monthly Federal Register Index (paper, purchased separately) is $29; annual subscription price for the monthly LSA (List of CFR Sections Affected) is $30 (paper, purchased separately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prices exclude postage; prevailing postal rates applied based on delivery method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution of the Federal Register within the government (§ 12.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the daily Federal Register in paper or microfiche shall be made available without charge to specified recipients — Members of Congress (each Senator/Member provided up to five copies upon written request), congressional committees (as needed upon written request), Supreme Court, other courts, and executive agencies (based on written requests) — and agencies may request overruns or extras under specified procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request overruns for special distribution, agencies must submit an advance printing and binding requisition on Standard Form 1 by 12 noon the working day before publication; agencies may order limited extra copies for official use from Superintendent of Documents; copies of Federal Register Index and LSA included with each official distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution of the Code of Federal Regulations within the government (§ 12.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the CFR in paper or microfiche shall be made available without charge to congressional committees, the Supreme Court, other courts, and executive agencies (not to exceed 300 copies of individual titles per agency) based on written requests; legislative, judicial, and executive agencies may obtain additional copies at cost by submitting requisitions pre-press or from the Superintendent after press run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits on free copies (e.g., 300 copies per agency per title) and procedures for obtaining extra copies are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution of The United States Government Manual (§ 12.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the Manual shall be made available without charge to Members of Congress (each Senator/Member provided twelve copies), congressional committees (as needed), Supreme Court (not more than 18 copies), other courts (one copy), and each head of a Federal executive agency and each liaison officer (one copy); additional copies may be obtained at cost pre-press or purchased after press run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific quantity allocations for recipients and requisition/payment procedures provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution of Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents (§ 12.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the Weekly Compilation shall be made available without charge to Members of Congress, congressional committees, Supreme Court, other courts, and executive agencies (with written requests); agencies may obtain additional copies at cost by pre-press requisition; after press run, extra copies must be paid for to Superintendent of Documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures parallel those for other official distributions; advance arrangements required for overruns of separate part issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution of Public Papers of the Presidents (§ 12.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the Public Papers shall be made available without charge to Members of Congress (each Member provided one copy of each annual publication during the Member's term upon written request), the Supreme Court (not more than 12 copies), and each head of a Federal executive agency (one copy); additional copies available at cost pre-press or for purchase after press run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written request procedures and pre-press requisition processes apply; after-press purchases addressed to Superintendent of Documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director assistance and cooperation to agencies (§ 15.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall assist each agency in complying with the pertinent publication laws to assure efficient public service in promulgating administrative documents having the effect of legal notice or of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistance is aimed at ensuring efficient promulgation of documents that provide legal notice or effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information services provided by the Office (§ 15.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall provide for the answering of each appropriate inquiry presented in person, by telephone, or in writing; each written communication and each matter involving the Administrative Committee shall be sent to the Director at the Office of the Federal Register, NARA, Washington, DC 20408.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies modes of inquiry response and mailing address for written communications and Administrative Committee matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff assistance for drafting and promulgation (§ 15.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff of the Office of the Federal Register shall provide informal assistance and advice to agency officials with respect to general or specific programs of regulatory drafting, procedures, and promulgation practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal technical and procedural advice is available to agency officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction and certification of copies (§ 15.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall furnish to requesting agencies, at cost, reproductions or certified copies of original acts and documents filed with that Office that are needed for official use unless funds are appropriated for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Furnishing reproductions/certified copies is charged at cost absent appropriated funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and instruction on drafting and publication (§ 15.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may prepare and distribute to agencies information and instructions designed to promote effective compliance with chapter 15 of title 44, sections 552–553 of title 5, related statutes, and this chapter, and may develop and conduct programs of technical instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may create guidance and training programs to improve agency compliance with publication and notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of agency representatives (§ 16.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall designate persons to serve as a liaison officer and alternate, a certifying officer and alternate, and an authorizing officer and alternate; the same person may serve in one or more positions; agencies must notify the Director of the name, title, address, and telephone number of each designated person and promptly notify the Director of any changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In choosing a liaison officer, agencies should select someone directly involved in the agency's regulatory program because the liaison will be the main contact with the Office and charged with duties in § 16.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison officer duties (§ 16.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency liaison officer shall: (a) represent the agency in all matters relating to submission of documents to the Office and general compliance with this chapter; (b) be responsible for effective distribution and use within the agency of Federal Register information on drafting and publication assistance authorized by § 15.10; (c) promote the agency's participation in technical instruction authorized by § 15.10; and (d) be available to discuss documents submitted for publication with editors of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaison is the main agency contact for submissions, internal dissemination of FR guidance, training promotion, and editorial discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifying officer duties (§ 16.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency certifying officer is responsible for attaching the required number of true copies of each original document submitted by the agency to the Office of the Federal Register and for making the certification required by §§ 18.5 and 18.6 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifying officer ensures required true copies are attached and requisite certifications are made per referenced sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing receipt/processing hours and confidentiality (§ 17.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless special arrangements are made with the Director, the Office of the Federal Register receives documents only during official working hours; upon receipt, each document shall be held for confidential processing until it is filed for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal receipt limited to working hours; documents are confidential until filed for public inspection unless special arrangements exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authorizing officer responsibilities: mailing lists (intro to § 17.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency authorizing officer is responsible for furnishing to the Director a current mailing list of officers or employees of the agency who are authorized to receive the Federal Register, the Code of Federal Regulations, and the Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must maintain and provide current lists of authorized recipients to the Director to control official distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timing for regular schedule (§ 17.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document received shall be filed for public inspection only after it has been received, processed, and assigned a publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents are not filed for public inspection until processing complete and publication date assigned; regular schedule procedures and timing govern publication assignments.
